contexts: regional orthopaedic centre, about 1,900 joint replacements a year
screening at pre-assessment three to four weeks before surgery
patients up to two hours away
reading: A pathway has five parts that the retrieved records show vary: the screening point, the referral trigger, the clinic lead, the treatment and its location, and communication with the patient. The screening point sets the time available for treatment; triggers and ownership decide who is referred and who acts. Existing reports describe these parts poorly. Distance to treatment shapes whether distant patients can complete it.
